answer: Echo-spiral routing cost: each identity must originate routes that return through a widening spiral of distinct relay neighborhoods, and a whisper channel carries only signed hop receipts. Nodes admit traffic only when its spiral revisits no prior neighborhood, so a sybil farm’s shared hosting footprint collapses every candidate path onto one mesa of overlapping relays. An attacker must then lease genuinely separate network positions per identity and sustain real forwarding load across them, paying recurring bandwidth and relay rents rather than a one-time fee.
